reconcile.note: Gill reads John 5:29's 'good' as grace-enabled faith-obedience in believers, not natural virtue, leaving Paul's total-depravity verdict on the unconverted untouched.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Robert G. Ingersoll catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Robert G. Ingersoll, Heretics and Heresies (1874).

sides.snippet: those who have done good, to the resurrection of life
sides.verseText: and will come out; those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment.

sides.snippet: There is no one who does good, No, not, so much as one.
sides.verseText: They have all turned aside. They have together become unprofitable. There is no one who does good, No, not, so much as one.\"
